title: Spike throttler and KV reservoir for GPU memory safety under high QPS
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: In high QPS scenarios we observe transient request surges that simultaneously increase micro-batch sizes and KV cache pressure, leading to GPU OOMs and long tail latency spikes. Existing admission controllers react using a single global headroom estimate which is brittle: it either throttles too early (harm to throughput) or too late (OOMs and retries).

Goal: Implement a low-latency 'spike throttler' that combines a lightweight reservoir for KV cache allocations with demand-aware microbatch admission so that short-lived spikes are absorbed without permanent throughput degradation. The feature should preserve tail-latency SLOs (p99 latency target for interactive API routes) and reduce emergency KV evictions under bursty load.

Design summary:
- KV reservoir: maintain a small, time-decayed reservation pool of KV bytes per-GPU (soft-reserve). On an incoming request, estimate its expected KV footprint (using model metadata + recent sequence length histogram) and charge against the reservoir first. If the reservoir can cover it, admit immediately with no batch growth. If not, check admission rules below. Reservoir refills gradually based on observed idle GPU time and successful microbatch completions.
- Spike throttler admission: add a fast-path admission check that runs before the main admission loop. It computes a short-window QPS derivative and, combined with reservoir usage, decides between: immediate admit, enqueue for microbatching, or shed (fail-fast with a 429 and retry-backoff signal).
- Soft headroom adjustments: instead of a single global headroom per GPU, track two headrooms: (1) steady-state headroom for autoscaler signals and long-running behavior, (2) transient headroom used by the spike throttler and reservoir. Transient headroom allows temporary growth without impacting long-term allocations.
- KV eviction grace windows: when eviction is triggered, use a prioritized eviction policy that prefers cold prefixes and voluntary prefetch cancellation for long-running conversations. Evictions triggered by reservoir exhaustion are treated as 'low severity' and avoid aggressive full-cache wipes.

Trade-offs considered:
- Complexity vs latency: Reservoir accounting must be extremely cheap (few atomic ops) to avoid adding latency to the admission path. We use per-GPU ring counters with eventual consistency to minimize cross-thread coordination.
- Fairness: Short reservation windows bias toward recent requests. To avoid starvation of background workloads, controller considers a background-weight factor that scales reservoir charges for non-interactive routes.
- Accuracy of KV footprint estimates: We'll initially use a conservative estimator (sequence length + tokenization overhead) with a future hook for ML-based estimators. Conservative estimates reduce OOM risk but may increase shedding.
acceptance_criteria: No GPU OOM incidents in the canary cluster under synthetic surge tests (100k RPS 30s spikes) for two consecutive runs
p99 latency for interactive-chat routes does not regress by more than 10% under steady-state load
Number of emergency KV evictions during a 30s surge drops by >= 60% compared to baseline
Feature gated and controllable via runtime flags and per-customer routing policy
Observability: dashboards for reservoir utilization, spike-throttler decisions, and per-GPU transient headroom
notes: This ticket focuses on runtime admission and KV behavior; autoscaler/placement changes are out-of-scope but will be handled by follow-ups. We intentionally separate transient headroom from autoscaler signals to avoid thrashing the scaler during short bursts.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1: implement per-GPU reservoir counters and cheap footprint estimator (3d). Phase 2: fast-path spike detector and admission hook (4d). Phase 3: eviction grace window policy and prioritized eviction (3d). Phase 4: canary rollout + metrics + rollback (2d). Total ~12 work-days.

Instrumentation: add Prometheus metrics: reservoir_capacity_bytes, reservoir_used_bytes, spike_derivative_qps, admits_by_path{fast_path,main,enqueued,shed}, eviction_reasons{reservoir,pressure,manual}. Add trace spans around admission decisions (for distributed tracing).

Testing: unit tests for reservoir arithmetic, integration tests with synthetic clients simulating sequence-length distributions, and chaos test (random OOM inductions) in staging.

Rollout plan: feature flag -> internal canary (10% infra) -> customer canary with opt-in -> default on for non-critical tiers. Immediate rollback via flag if p99 latency or OOMs regress.
